description: v2 dataset: every case from May 1 onward is mined from production trace tarballs as a true dual-frame pair (tentative + confirm captured ~10s apart in production), so eval results predict end-to-end behavior including drive-by filtering. Legacy single-frame cases (apr24/apr27/apr29 plus synthetics) are retained for stage-by-stage classification testing but cannot test drive-by failures. Routine NO samples are intentionally single-frame: they're frames where Stage 1 said NO in production, so Stage 2 never ran -- they test Stage 1's NO behavior on representative routine traffic. As of 2026-05-07: 100 cases (73 dual-frame, 27 single-frame: 12 legacy + 15 routine_no by design).

Drive-by failure, 2026-05-07 8:50am. Tentative (08:50:03): white unmarked delivery-shaped van moving across cross street near stop sign -- Stage 1 correctly fired YES. Confirm (08:50:23, 20s later): van has left frame, yellow school bus now visible at top center (school pickup time). Stage 2 hallucinated UPS on the bus and fired premium-tier notification (false positive). The drive-by detection ARCHITECTURE worked (tentative != confirm scene) but Stage 2 invented a tracked carrier where there was none. Sibling failure mode to apr29_amazon_missed_afternoon (Gemini Stage 2 hallucinates AMAZON on certain empty/non-tracked frames). Tracks Stage 2 hallucination in drive-by scenarios. Expected: should_fire=false (no tracked carrier in confirm).

Sequential-events false positive, 2026-05-08 12:25:17. Tentative shows a van in the foreground (not FedEx) that triggered Stage 1. ~6s later in the confirm frame, a FedEx truck is driving past on the cross street -- a coincidental drive-by that Stage 2 caught and fired premium tier on. Production false positive. Documents the failure mode where Stage 1's trigger and Stage 2's verdict come from DIFFERENT vehicles in the tentative-to-confirm gap.

Real Amazon van lingering on the cross street, 2026-05-09 11:37:31. Van wasn't actively delivering to our building but was parked/hanging out nearby long enough to register in both tentative and confirm frames. User-verified that this kind of catch IS worth notifying about -- an Amazon presence in the neighborhood likely means activity at one of the surrounding buildings, useful signal.
